First, it correctly lists the approximate masses (proton ≈ 1.007 u, neutron ≈ 1.009 u, electron ≈ 0.00055 u) and correctly identifies that an electron has the smallest mass. However, in the decision section, it incorrectly concludes that the "smallest mass loss comes from losing a proton" and claims the electron is "heavier" because 31 > 27. This is mathematically false (10^-31 is much smaller than 10^-27) and physically incorrect regarding the masses of these particles. Since the conclusion (A) contradicts the data provided in the same step and the actual physics, this step leads to an incorrect solution.
